points.claim: Daenerys posed an ongoing threat, but she was not attacking at the moment I struck.
points.support: The record shows the city had surrendered and organized resistance had ceased. She was unarmed and not actively harming anyone when I killed her, so the immediate danger required to justify lethal force was absent.

points.claim: I did not exhaust safer options before resorting to lethal action.
points.support: I never convened a council, attempted detention, or sought a public surrender of power. The record notes I made no effort to rally other leaders or contain her through less harmful means, which undermines any claim of necessity.

points.claim: I lacked the authority to execute her, and the killing denied any form of trial.
points.support: I am not a judge, nor do I hold any official warrant to sentence anyone. My lack of formal authority, combined with the absence of a judicial process, means the act cannot be justified as lawful enforcement.

points.claim: I used our intimacy to get close enough to strike, which was a breach of trust.
points.support: I exploited our personal relationship to approach her without warning. This deception shows the act was not a spontaneous defense but a calculated killing, further undermining any justification.
